Hi Avery,

Thanks for taking this meeting last week — follow-up from our product team. We are evaluating a hybrid approach for our semantic search stack: primary embedding store on S3 (cold archive/backfill) plus pgvector for fast local-ish queries, with Pinecone as a fallback/managed read tier for high-throughput spikes.

Attached is a short map of our existing architecture and an interoperability checklist (nimbus-interop-map.pdf, interoperability-checklist.xlsx). High-level asks:
- Can Redwood route queries by cost/latency between S3/pgvector/Pinecone?
- What are recommended fallthrough and consistency strategies for eventual reindex flows?
- Any constraints around encryption-at-rest or KV cache behavior we should be aware of?

We have a HubSpot record (HS-3241-NIM) and would like to set a pilot with clear SLOs if this looks feasible. Can you loop in the right folks on your side?

Best,

Hi Elaine — thanks for the detail and for the attachments, they were helpful. Looping in Vanessa (partner GTM), Marissa (solutions / deal lead), and Karthik (tech partner) to scope technical/ops and commercial next steps.

Quick answers to your bullets:
- Short: yes — Redwood can route by policy (latency-first, cost-first, region affinity) and has configurable fallbacks to compatible model/index variants when capacity shifts. We support automatic prefix/KV caching and configurable cache TTLs to reduce S3 reads when the same queries recur.
- Reindex flows: common pattern is write-through to pgvector for hot vectors + async backfill to S3 for cold. We recommend a short warm window (48–72h) before evicting from hot tier in high-churn workloads.
- Encryption: we support customer-managed KMS for all host types (S3, pgvector on-host, and integrations with partner vaults); Karthik can confirm exact handshake for pgvector deployments.

Next steps I propose:
1) 30-min technical sync (Karthik + Elaine + Nimbus eng) to capture expected QPS, index sizes, and dim/format constraints.
2) Pilot SOW: 6-week pilot with a scoped dataset and rolling SLA targets (p99 read latency target, throughput burst profile).
3) Commercial: Marissa will provide a light commercial proposal and pilot pricing once we have the dataset numbers.

Marissa — will you pick this up for the SOW + pricing? Karthik — can you prepare a short config checklist and questions for the sync?

Avery

Hi Elaine — thanks for sharing the artifacts. I reviewed the map and checklist and have a few targeted technical questions so we can size the pilot correctly:

1) Expected sustained QPS and expected spike factor (example: sustained 200 qps, spikes x5).
2) Typical vector dimension and encoded dtype (float32/float16/int8/quantized).
3) Current index sizes (GB/TB) and average vector count per document.
4) Cold data lifecycle: how long before items are eligible for S3 cold-tier (days)?
5) Encryption: if you need HSM-backed keys for pgvector nodes we should flag that early.
6) Any locality constraints (must keep EU data in EU) — helps with routing policy.

Preliminary config suggestions (high level):
- Hot tier: pgvector cluster with prefix caching (kv-cache) and async write-through to S3.
- Mid-tier / fallback: Pinecone managed index for high-throughput bursts (we can route reads to Pinecone when local QPS exceeds threshold or latency SLO is at risk).
- Cold-tier: S3 with object index metadata in Redwood for lazy rehydrate on demand.

I attached a short checklist that maps config knobs to pilot acceptance criteria. Happy to go through each item on a call.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer — Integrations
Redwood Inference
